description_text: Worker Type Regular Job Description Summary The Senior Quality Control Engineer (QE) is accountable for the overall delivered quality of products and/or services to customers and ensures quality controls are met. Position Responsibilities: Quality Planning and Engineering: Develop and implement comprehensive quality assurance and quality control plans for CUAS components and systems. Define quality metrics, testing methodologies, and inspection procedures to ensure adherence to quality standards throughout the product lifecycle. Review manufacturing planning to align quality control points and data collection. Coordinate work with Quality Technicians and inspectors as necessary Collaborate with cross-functional teams to ensure robust manufacturing processes and work instructions are in place, and that inspection and test gates (incoming, in-process, and final) are defined at the appropriate stages of the build. Perform process capabilities analysis on key characteristics; implementing Inspection and Quality Plans Ensure product acceptance criteria reflects the customer's definition of fitness for use Review customer contracts and purchase orders to identify requirements and flow down new customer requirements to all functions Correspond, as required, with customer representatives to ensure a thorough understanding of their needs and expectations Collaborate with engineering teams to establish quality requirements, specifications, and standards for new product development. Perform risk assessments and analysis on designs to identify potential quality and reliability risks, and develop mitigation strategies to address them. Worker Type Regular Job Description Summary The Principal GNC Engineer will be responsible for delivering advanced GNC solutions for the VAPOR uncrewed rotorcraft system. This role ensures program engineering needs are met by leading the design, analysis, and implementation of GNC algorithms and related software, and by planning and executing the integration of components into complete flight systems. The Principal GNC Engineer tackles broad, complex technical challenges, develops new GNC and software technologies, and drives innovative control solutions from concept through deployment for novel rotorcraft platforms. This role encompasses a multi-disciplinary background to include GNC (60%), Software (25%), flight testing (5%), and other projects (10%). This role helps lead development of technical proposals and project estimates, drives technical and engineering conflicts to resolution and ensures the engineering needs of their assigned product development projects are met. As an expert in the field, one uses professional concepts in developing resolution to critical issues and broad design matters. title: Scientist – Materials Characterization
description_text:
Worker Type Regular Job Description The Materials Characterization Facility (MCF) is seeking a highly motivated Staff Scientist to join our advanced microscopy team. This role is designed as a growth-oriented position, offering the unique opportunity to work at the cutting edge of electron optics while receiving direct mentorship from senior research staff to develop world-class technical mastery. The successful candidate will bridge the gap between high-end instrument operation and active research development, focusing on the characterization of advanced electronic devices and material defects. A key pillar of this role involves leveraging state-of-the-art software to develop automation routines that increase facility throughput and data precision. Key Responsibilities
1. Advanced Electron Microscopy & Spectroscopy Expert Operation: Provide primary technical support and high-level operation of Transmission Electron Microscopes (TEM/STEM). Analytical Spectroscopy: Execute and interpret complex chemical and structural analysis using EDS and EELS. Device Characterization: Perform detailed analysis of electronic devices, specifically targeting defect characterization, interfacial phenomena, and dopant/strain mapping. 2. Precision Sample Preparation FIB Operations: Utilize Focused Ion Beam (FIB) systems for the site-specific preparation of high-quality TEM lamellae. Advanced Thinning: Master in-situ lift-out and precision thinning/cleaning protocols to ensure optimal samples for aberration-corrected imaging. 3. Automation & Digital Innovation Routine Development: Develop and deploy custom automation routines using manufacturer APIs and scripting (e.g., Python, DM Script) to streamline data collection. Software Integration: Leverage state-of-the-art software suites (e.g., Velox, GMS3) to implement high-throughput workflows. Data Pipelines: Establish standardized processing pipelines to handle large datasets generated by high-speed detectors. 4. Research Partnership & Technique Development Direct Research Support: Partner with the research team to develop novel analytical techniques tailored to specific materials of interest. Methodology Innovation: Transition from executing established protocols to authoring new ones for beam-sensitive or complex heterostructured material Mentorship & Career Growth This position is structured to foster long-term professional development. The Staff Scientist will: Partner with senior scientists to acquire specialized technical intuition in advanced TEM and aberration-corrected microscopy. Be empowered to dedicate time to mastering new hardware, such as in-situ biasing or heating holders. Grow into a technical leadership role within the facility, with opportunities for co-authorship on high-impact publications. Required Qualifications U.S. Citizenship required due to the nature of the work and customer requirements. Ph.D. or M.S. in Materials Science, Physics, Electrical Engineering, or a related field. Proven experience with TEM/STEM imaging and diffraction. Functional knowledge of EDS and EELS data acquisition and quantification. Hands-on experience with FIB-based TEM lamella preparation (lift-out). Proficiency (or strong aptitude) in Python or similar scripting for data manipulation. Preferred Skills Experience with electronic device failure analysis and defect engineering. Familiarity with 4D-STEM or other emerging electron optic modalities. Strong communication skills and a desire to work in a collaborative, multi-disciplinary environment. The primary responsibility of this role is to be the lead for all repairs, warranty, service, and upgrade hardware activities. More specifically it is to handle returned hardware (e.g. under RMA, warranty, or defect management processes), diagnose, troubleshoot, repair and test units to ensure they meet quality and performance standards. The technician will work closely with mechanical, electrical, and systems engineers, and must have strong capabilities in debugging and working with advanced electronics and hardened computing systems. You will need to be comfortable working through ambiguity and change and also be intellectually curious regarding hardware and electronics assembly and manufacturing. title: Wet Lab Protein Engineer (Selective Molecular Recognition)
description_text: Worker Type Regular Job Description Position Overview AV and the AFRL Biological Materials and Processing Research Team are seeking a Protein Engineer to spearhead the directed evolution and screening pipelines of proteins for high-affinity ion coordination. This role will generate diverse protein libraries, develop robust high-throughput screening (HTS) assays, and isolate variants with selectivity and affinity for specific Rare Earth Elements. The candidate will collaborate with the Computational Design Team. The core mission of this role is to produce and screen computationally designed proteins and use results to improve the next round of directed evolution. Additionally, this role will support the scale up of protein production and integration into pilot-scale commercial applications. Key Responsibilities Translate Computational Designs to the Bench: Serve as the primary bridge between dry-lab and wet-lab operations; take candidate designs, scaffolds, and libraries generated by the computational biology team and successfully translate them into physical, high-diversity protein libraries. Library Construction & Directed Evolution: Generate protein/peptide libraries using advanced molecular biology techniques High-Throughput Screening & Selection: Develop and execute robust, automated HTS assays (such as cell-surface display or plate-based fluorimetry) to screen designs for highly selective Rare Earth Element (REE) binding, successfully isolating rare "hit" variants from background noise. Data Integration & Loop Closure: Analyze screening data to identify sequence-activity relationships. You will feed this high-quality experimental data back to the computational design team to validate their predictive models, troubleshoot failures, and guide the design of the next, smarter round of directed evolution. Assay Optimization: Continually refine screening pressures (pH, competing transition metals, lanthanide concentrations) to ensure the assay environment accurately reflects industrial bio-purification conditions. Test assay environments with candidate protein variants "hits" at pilot-scale levels. Required Qualifications Education: Ph.D. in Chemistry, Biochemistry, Molecular Biology, Bioengineering Biophysics, or a related field. (Candidates with an M.S. and 4+ years of high-throughput engineering will be considered). Protein Engineering: Design, optimize, and characterize proteins and biologics using state-of-the-art molecular biology and high-throughput screening techniques. The Material Control Specialist II is responsible for maintaining optimal inventory levels to support production and operational efficiency while adhering to company policies and procedures. This role involves tracking, analyzing, and reconciling inventory records to ensure accuracy and availability. The Material Control Specialist collaborates with procurement, production, and warehouse teams to optimize inventory flow and minimize discrepancies. Position Responsibilities Monitors inventory levels and ensures materials are available to meet production and operational needs. Receives and counts stock items, and records data using computerized system. Packs and unpacks items to be stocked on shelves in stockroom in an orderly and accessible manner. Conducts cycle counts and physical inventory audits to reconcile stock discrepancies. Investigates and resolves inventory variances by working closely with procurement, warehouse, and production teams. Issues or distributes materials, products, parts, and supplies to customers or coworkers, based on information from incoming requisitions. Maintains accurate inventory records in the ERP/MRP system, ensuring data integrity. Depending on warehouse, some positions may also be responsible for packaging and shipping (domestic and international -- to include small package, large freight, dangerous goods and sensitive items). Collaborates with suppliers and internal stakeholders to track incoming shipments and expedite critical materials when necessary. Assists in implementing inventory control policies, procedures and process improvements to enhance inventory efficiency and reduce waste. Works on assignments that are semi-routine in nature but recognizes the need for occasional deviation from accepted practice. Performs other duties as assigned by supervisors or inventory managers. Other duties as assigned Basic Qualifications (Required Skills & Experience) Minimum of 1 – 2 years of related functional experience (i.e.- previous stockroom/inventory) or equivalent combination of experience and education. High School diploma or GED equivalent is required. Foundational knowledge of inventory management principles and warehouse operations. Proficiency in MS Office Suite (Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Outlook). Experience working with MRP/ERP systems for inventory tracking and control. Demonstrated computer skills and proficiency using office software and/or computerized inventory control system. A valid driver's license and clean driving record is required in order to drive company vehicles. Other Qualifications & Desired Competencies APICS Certification (CPIM) or equivalent is desirable but not required. Experience using Oracle ERP or a similar system is preferred. Forklift experience desirable but not required. Prior Hazmat shipping experience (lithium-ion or equivalent) is desired. Demonstrated knowledge of safe material handling practices and the safe handling of electro-static sensitive components (ESD) is desired. Strong analytical and problem-solving skills with attention to detail. Ability to work effectively in a fast-paced, deadline-driven environment. Excellent interpersonal and communication skills for collaboration across departments. Highly organized with the ability to prioritize multiple tasks and meet deadlines. Demonstrates initiative, accountability, and continuous improvement mindset. Physical Demands Ability to work in an office and warehouse/manufacturing environment (Constant). Regularly required to stand, walk, sit, talk, hear, and use hands and fingers to operate a computer/mobile device and handle inventory (Constant). May operate dolly, pallet jack and/or forklift in loading and unloading supplies and equipment (Occasional). Ability to lift up to 60 lbs. and objects of varying sizes and shapes (Occasional). title: Senior Systems Engineer

Worker Type Regular Job Description AV is seeking skilled Systems Engineers to support the design, development, integration, testing, and deployment of advanced electromechanical, opto-mechanical, and RF systems across our diverse portfolio of defense solutions. In this role, you will be a key technical contributor on programs spanning ground, air, and space domains --working at the intersection of multiple engineering disciplines to ensure system-level success. As a Systems Engineer, you will lead requirements management, architecture definition, interface control, and verification planning for complex, multi-disciplinary systems. You will collaborate closely with mechanical, electrical, software, and test teams to integrate subsystems into mission-capable solutions, manage technical risks, and ensure our systems meet customer performance, schedule, and cost objectives. This position offers the opportunity to work on cutting-edge technologies supporting critical national security missions, with exposure to multiple domains and program phases. You will contribute to AV's reputation for innovation and technical excellence while developing your systems engineering expertise in a fast-paced, mission-focused environment. Ideal candidates bring a strong foundation in systems engineering principles, hands-on experience with end-to-end system development and hardware-software integration, excellent communication skills, and the ability to thrive in a collaborative, cross-functional team setting. title: Principal Digital Engineering Systems Architect
location: 410 Jan Davis Drive NorthWest, Huntsville, AL
description_text: Worker Type Regular Job Description AV is seeking a Principal Digital Engineering Systems Architect to guide and execute Digital Engineering strategy for the Kinetic Interceptors team across a portfolio of advanced missile programs. This senior technical leadership role focuses on the development and integration of model-based systems engineering (MBSE) practices, toolsets, and architectures to support end-to-end product development, analysis, and testing in a Digital Engineering environment. Key Responsibilities: Define and lead the Digital Engineering vision, strategy, and roadmap aligned with program and customer goals. Ensure technical integrity and execution across multi-disciplinary teams, driving solutions that meet or exceed cost, schedule, and performance requirements. Serve as the primary technical interface to senior DoD customers, program leadership, subcontractors, and partners. Architect and implement engineering ontologies, modeling patterns, and integration strategies across tools and platforms. Design and manage system architecture models supporting full lifecycle development --from concept to production. Lead a team of systems engineers in implementing MBSE best practices and advancing AV's Digital Engineering capabilities. Develop custom scripts and integrations to optimize workflows and model validations across tools. Support and maintain existing Digital Engineering tool customizations, triage technical issues, and implement corrective actions. Collaborate with stakeholders to assess business needs and translate them into scalable engineering solutions. Generate clear technical specifications and documentation. Mentor junior engineers and help build technical depth across the organization. Basic Qualifications: B.S. in an engineering discipline with 12+ years of experience, M.S. with 10+ years, or Ph.D. with 8+ years. Minimum of 5 years of experience developing and leading Digital Engineering environments in support of weapon systems. An active Secret level security clearance. Strong background in system architecture design, systems engineering, integration, and testing. Demonstrated leadership in multi-disciplinary teams and experience managing technical execution across complex programs. Direct experience working with DoD customers and defense industry partners. Proven ability to manage multi-million-dollar engineering budgets and resources. Strong interpersonal, communication, and problem-solving skills. Experience with engineering Risk and Opportunity (R&O) management. Willingness to travel occasionally to customer or test sites. Preferred Qualifications: M.S. with 13+ years or Ph.D. with 11+ years of relevant experience. 10+ years of experience leading Digital Engineering efforts for complex defense systems. Hands-on experience with MBSE tools (e.g., Cameo, Rhapsody, Enterprise Architect) and data exchange mechanisms. title: Research Scientist – Physical Organic Chemistry and Materials Characterization
description_text: Worker Type Regular Job Description AV is seeking an entry-level Research Scientist to join our multidisciplinary team at the Air Force Research Laboratory (AFRL). The Polymers and Responsive Materials Team is seeking a highly versatile and computationally-fluent scientist to work at the intersection of Physical Organic Chemistry and Materials Physics. This role is designed for a researcher who thrives on applying advanced analytical toolkits, ranging from AI/ML to advanced spectroscopy techniques, across a diverse portfolio of research initiatives. As a key member of our lab, you will not be siloed into a single project. Instead, you will provide the digital-first characterization and mechanistic evaluation necessary to advance materials discovery for extreme environments, bio-inspired elastomers, and autonomous laboratory workflows. You will drive the characterization and data-driven analysis for several high-impact research areas, including: Space Survivability: Investigating how extreme stressors, such as atomic oxygen and ionizing radiation, interact with and degrade organic surfaces. Hierarchical Materials: Mapping the nanostructure and self-assembly of peptide-based synthetic rubbers and hybrid polymers. Closed-Loop Discovery: Integrating laboratory hardware with AI/ML optimization to automate the discovery of resilient, functional materials. PRIMARY RESPONSIBILITIES: Advanced Spectroscopy: Use XPS, FTIR, and NMR to identify molecular-level degradation pathways. Structural Physics: Design and execute experiments at synchrotron facilities using Small-Angle X-ray Scattering (SAXS/WAXS) to probe the morphology of soft matter. Digital Integration: Leverage Python to automate data processing from complex analytical instruments and implement AI/ML models for performance prediction. Mechanical Characterization: Correlate chemical changes with macro-scale performance through DMA, tensile testing, and rheological analysis. Hardware Innovation: Modify or build experimental hardware interfaces using open-source tools to enable automated, high-throughput characterization. REQUIREMENTS This position requires working within a government facility and requires U.S. Citizenship Education: MS or PhD in Chemistry, Polymer Science, Materials Science, Physics, or a related field with 0-1 years of experience Digital Proficiency: Strong proficiency in Python for data analysis, modeling, or laboratory automation. Analytical Depth: Expertise in spectroscopy and a strong foundational understanding of physical organic chemistry or polymer physics. Worker Type Regular Job Description Summary
The Senior Quality Engineer (QE) is accountable for delivered product quality to customers and for ensuring effective quality controls across the product lifecycle. The QE partners with program, product, and operations teams to eliminate cost and flow disruptions, implement visual factory KPIs, and lead robust problem reporting and CAPA for nonconformances. This role includes both customer‑facing quality and internal product quality responsibilities. Position Responsibilities Quality Planning and Engineering Develop and implement comprehensive quality assurance and quality control plans for components and systems across the product lifecycle.

Review manufacturing planning to align quality control points and data collection.
Coordinate work with Quality Technicians and Inspectors as necessary.
Perform process capability analysis on key characteristics and implement inspection and quality plans.
Ensure product acceptance criteria reflect the customer's definition of fitness for use.
Review customer contracts and purchase orders, flow down quality requirements, and collaborate with customer representatives to ensure mutual understanding of requirements and expectations.
Collaborate with engineering teams to establish quality requirements, specifications, and standards for new product development.
Provide input on Design for Manufacturability (DFM) and Design for Assembly (DFA) to optimize product quality and efficiency.
Perform risk assessments and analysis on designs to identify potential quality and reliability risks, and develop mitigation strategies.
Utilize tools such as Failure Mode and Effects Analysis (FMEA) to systematically assess and prioritize risks and develop appropriate risk mitigation plans.
Participate in Product Readiness Reviews (PRR) and coordinate Final Inspection activities.
Participate in the review of engineering specifications to ensure the inclusion of adequate quality and reliability requirements.

Coordinate cross‑functional MRB meetings (Quality, Engineering, Operations, Supply Chain) to drive data‑based disposition decisions and prevent recurrence of known defects.

Drive corrective action and failure analysis in a timely manner.

Experience with creating and documenting Dimensional data packs and First Article Inspection Reports (FAIs). title: Target Analyst Reporter L2
description_text: Worker Type Regular Job Description Summary The Target Analyst Reporter is responsible for synthesizing intelligence from a variety of sources to provide actionable products for our customers. This role focuses on prioritizing, assessing, and evaluating information obtained through both passive and active collection, as well as network analysis. Working under the guidance of senior personnel, you will integrate raw intelligence with collateral data to produce reports that inform national security decisions. This is an ideal role for an analyst with strong foundational SIGINT knowledge who is looking to refine their reporting expertise within a mission-critical environment. Responsibilities Prioritize and evaluate information from active and passive collection and network analysis to create comprehensive intelligence products. Draft and refine intelligence reports, ensuring information is accurate, relevant, and formatted according to established policies. Use basic and advanced queries to locate reportable information within SIGINT and collateral repositories. description_text: Worker Type Regular Job Description Summary The Environmental Health & Safety Analyst will partner with EHS team members, production leaders and cross-functional team leaders to improve workplace performance by assessing work environments, systems, processes, and procedures. title: Senior Scientist- Advanced in vitro Systems Research
description_text:
Worker Type Regular Job Description AV has an opportunity for a Senior Scientist within the Health and Performance Technologies Division. This is an onsite position supporting the Air and Space Biosciences division of the 711th Human Performance Wing, located on Wright-Patterson AFB in Dayton OH. This position will lead and execute in vitro research programs utilizing microphysiological systems (MPS), new approach methodologies (NAMs), and advanced human-relevant cellular models to improve human health and performance, with a specific application towards Airmen and Guardians. The ideal candidate will have strong hands-on expertise in mammalian cell culture, experimental execution, and interdisciplinary collaboration within a fast-paced research environment. They will be responsible for working within the team to perform various assays, such as next-generation sequencing library preparation, microelectrode array, cytokine/inflammatory analysis, and other in vitro assays. The successful candidate will be an independent self-starter, have excellent organizational and time management skills, demonstrable written and oral communication skills, and thrive in a collaborative, team-based environment. Key responsibilities include: Lead, execute, and analyze in vitro experiments involving MPS and NAM-based platforms. Specific experience with brain models (iPSC-derived brain cells, BBB, microelectrode array) is highly preferred.
Characterize and assess various MPS using in vitro assays to measure neuronal function, cell viability, barrier function, and metabolic activity, as well as other cellular functions.
Maintenance, expansion, and experimental manipulation of mammalian tissue culture systems (e.g., iPSCs, primary cells, immortalized cell lines, organoids) using aseptic techniques.
Generate high-quality, reproducible datasets and maintain detailed experimental documentation.
Contribute to experimental design, protocol development, technical reports, presentations, and scientific publications.
Coordinate and collaborate with internal teams, external collaborators, and government scientists to ensure timely delivery of research products. Qualifications: Ph.D. in a biological discipline, such as Biology, Molecular Biology, Biochemistry, Molecular Genetics, Microbiology, or Immunology. 3+ years of experience in the MPS field is highly desired.
A strong background in in vitro systems, with hands-on experience in mammalian cellular and microbial culture, and advanced laboratory techniques (flow cytometry, microscopy, etc.). Previous experience with MPS/Organ-on-chip and stem cells/iPSCs is highly desired.
Data analysis skills, with proven ability to process and interpret complex data. Biostatistics experience is desired.

In this role, you will own the cost, schedule, and technical performance of the electrical hardware scope, leading a cross‑functional team to deliver compliant products on time and within budget under an EVMS environment. You will coordinate closely with Systems, Mechanical, Firmware, Assembly, Integration and Test, and Program Management to plan and execute the subsystem work scope from requirements development through integration, test, and production support. Key Responsibilities Lead the Program Electrical Engineering/Subsystem IPT, reporting to program management.
Own the technical baseline for the subsystem: requirements allocation, architecture, design decisions, and interfaces.
Planning responsibility over the design, analysis, schematic/PCB development, prototyping, integration, and verification activities.
Drive risk and opportunity management: identify technical and programmatic risks, develop mitigation plans, and track through closure.
Lead and coordinate technical reviews (SRR, PDR, CDR, TRR, etc.) for the subsystem.
Define, plan, and maintain the Electrical Engineering Control Accounts, including Work Breakdown Structure (WBS), work packages, and planning packages.
Develop and manage detailed schedules, budgets, and resource plans for the assigned scope, to include identification of critical path activities and risk mitigation strategies.
Manage cost and schedule performance using Earned Value Management System (EVMS) metrics (CPI, SPI, ETC/EAC, variance analysis).
Prepare and present monthly Control Account Manager (CAM) reports, variance analysis reports (VARs), and recovery plans to program leadership and the customer.
Support internal and customer reviews (e.g., PMRs, PDRs, CDRs, surveillance audits) as the accountable owner for the Electrical Engineering control accounts.
Support make/buy decisions, supplier selection, SOW definition, and technical oversight of electrical hardware suppliers.
Work with Manufacturing and Test Engineering to ensure designs are producible, testable, and support yield and cost targets.
Support proposal efforts and change proposals: develop BOEs, schedules, and risk assessments for new or modified scope.
Some travel required (~20%). Required Skills and Education: Must have 10+ years of relevant experience in engineering management, including direct implementation of EVMS principles.
Bachelor’s degree in Electrical Engineering or equivalent relevant experience.
Demonstrated experience as a CAM or similar role with responsibility for cost and schedule performance under EVMS on a complex program.
Proven experience leading cross‑functional engineering teams or acting as an IPT/technical lead.
Strong understanding of full product life cycle: requirements, design, analysis, integration, test, and transition to production.
Demonstrated ability to interpret and act on cost/schedule metrics and to develop credible recovery plans.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills; comfortable presenting to internal and customer leadership.
Proficiency in Microsoft Project, Excel, PowerPoint, and other program management tools (e.g., Jira, Gitlab, etc.).
Strong leadership and team‑building abilities; able to influence without direct authority.
High accountability for commitments, with a track record of delivering on cost/schedule/technical objectives.
Structured problem‑solving and root‑cause analysis skills.
Ability to operate effectively in a fast‑paced, matrixed organization.
Ability to obtain and maintain a U.S. DOD Clearance. Desired Skills and Education: Master’s degree in Electrical or Systems engineering.
Formal EVMS training and experience supporting customer EVMS/IBR reviews.
Experience leading efforts through major design reviews (SRR, PDR, CDR) and qualification/acceptance testing.
Experience with model‑based systems engineering (MBSE) and/or digital engineering environments.
